newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria wants Israeli gesture to resume talks.
newsitem.headline: Syria wants Israeli gesture to resume talks.

text.p: Syria has asked a European envoy on Wednesday to secure a goodwill gesture from the government of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to resume peace talks suspended for about a year.

Miguel Angel Moratinos, European Middle East envoy, told reporters the request was made by President Hafez al-Assad during talks in Damascus on Wednesday which centred on how to resume the talks which opened in Madrid in 1991.

"He asked me to get from the Israeli side some kind of gesture.. some kind of declaration of goodwill from the Netanyahu government.. and some kind of clarification on what they mean by resuming the talks on the basis of 242 and the Madrid principles," Moratinos said.

He said Assad and Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara were interested in remarks made recently by Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy in which he said Israel was ready to resume talks on the basis of Madrid conference and U.N. resolution 242.
Syrian officials say the interpretation of the current Likud-led Israeli government of resolution 242 did not mean full withdrawal from all the occupied Arab lands.

Syria which wants Israel to withdraw fully from the Golan Heights, captured by Israel from Syria in the 1967 Middle East war, had strongly condemned Netanyahu for refusing to swap the occupied Arab lands for peace.

No talks were held since he took office in June last year. the former Israeli government broke off talks with Syria in March 1996 after a wave of Islamic suicide bombings in Israel in which 59 people were killed.
The European envoy said he was proposing a new formula that would meet the concerns of both Syria and Israel especially withdrawal from the occupied lands, peace and security.
"I think Israel is very much concerned about security. I think we have to start to think about a formula that could include all elements...land...peace and security...
"Full withdrawal. full security could lead to full peace. I think that is the way that we are trying to work in the future," he said.
The European envoy said he was satisfied with the outcome of his talks with Assad but said he expected himself to be engaged in a long shuttle between Syria and Israel to narrow the gaps.
"I want to say that I found there is a great mistrust between the two sides. Israel and Syria. There is a lack of understanding of each sides' views and initiatives," Moratinos said.

"I was a long-distance runner when I was a youth. I am ready to run again for a long distance. I am prepared myself to be here and in Israel to convey this message of peace that is needed for the security and prosperity of the region," he said.
The European envoy said he would brief the United States and Russia, the co-sponsors of the Arab-Israeli peace talks, on the outcome of his discussions in Syria and Israel.
He also thanked President Assad for seeing him as the first foreign personality after recovering from a prostate surgery which was anounced on January 7.
